messages:
Kevin: Quick sync — we need a concrete proposal for the new pool telemetry fields for hosted + dedicated. Main asks: SM occupancy, per-GPU memory used, queue depth, queued latency percentiles, and per-pool headroom. Who owns dashboard & alerts?
Priya: I can lead the dashboard UX, but need stable metric names and tags. We should have tags: pool_id, pool_type (hosted|dedicated), region, instance_type, model_variant.
Jules: +1. For SM occupancy we should report both per-SM and aggregated per-GPU. Sample schema:
```
metric: redwood.gpu.sm_occupancy_pct
labels: pool_id, pool_type, gpu_index, sm_index, model_variant
value: float (0-100)
sample_rate: 1s
```
Samira: Queue depth metrics: redwood.gpu.queue_depth and redwood.gpu.queue_wait_ms with p50/p95/p99 histograms. Important for autoscaler signals.
Daniel: For dedicated pools we also need committed_capacity and reserved_slots metrics.
infra-bot: note: new metric registration requires PR to infra/telemetry repo; see: https://git.redwood/infra/telemetry
Priya: UX question — show dedicated vs hosted on same graph or separate tabs? I prefer same graph with toggle to avoid duplicate dashboards.
Kevin: Ops: add alerting suggestions. Suggested alert: sm_occupancy_pct p95 > 85% for 5m for two consecutive windows -> paging.
Jules: Also add unit labels for memory: bytes, and expose free_memory and total_memory per GPU.
Samira: Implementation plan: runtime emits per-request incr to queue_depth on enqueue, decr on dequeue; KV cache hits should be tagged to avoid inflating occupancy.
Priya: I'll draft a dashboard mock and permalinks for owners: Eng-Platform (Jules), DevEx (Priya). Can we get commit window next week?
Kevin: Let's do RFC PR by EOD Wednesday. @deploy-bot can you note this as a tracking ticket?
deploy-bot: created ticket T-1142: "Pool telemetry schema + dashboard RFC" assigned to Kevin, due 7 days
Jules: I'll start a telemetry PR with the metric names above and a prometheus histogram for queue_wait_ms. Will ping infra for sampling rate.
Priya: thanks — will also add short text in dashboard explaining differences between hosted/dedicated capacity.
Kevin: Great. If nobody objects, I'll mark this as the canonical plan and start the RFC doc.
